question: Where does the branch a pull request targets live — a config key read off the base ref, or the branch you happen to be standing on?

options.label: A `dispatch.base` key in .sober/config.jsonc
options.reason: Every other dispatch setting — host, setup, verify, draftPr, accept — is already a config key read off the base ref (docs/adr/0019-configuration-is-read-from-the-base.md, packages/core/src/config.ts). The target stops being an accident of what is checked out, it travels with the repository, and a second person who clones gets the same answer without being told.
options.costLater: The key that names the base is itself read from the base, so the very first read still has to fall back to the current branch — a bootstrap fold that has to be written and explained once, forever. A repository that renames its branch now has one more file to update.

options.label: Stay with the current branch, as today
options.reason: Nothing to build. `--base` already overrides it per invocation, and a person who stands on the right branch gets the right answer.
options.costLater: Every run started from `main` quietly targets `main`, which is exactly the release nobody asked for. The rule lives in a person's head instead of the repository, so it holds until the first tired evening.

options.label: Read origin/HEAD, git's own default branch
options.reason: git already records which branch is the default; no new setting, no new file, no drift between config and remote.
options.costLater: origin/HEAD names `main` — the one branch we specifically do not want as the everyday target — so it answers the wrong question. It is also unset in plenty of clones, which puts the fallback back where it started.
